overall_assessment: No personal data is left. The only staff names in the raw text (5 'Emneansvarlig' blocks) are stripped by .anon_oslomet(), there are no e-mails or phone numbers, and every span removed in the packet is an admin year, a semester or cohort label, an approval date or a bare ';' line, so nothing in the sample is over-removed. The pre-pass flags are false alarms: all 56 name_label hits are the pre-pass regex reading 'naturfaglærer' + 'Innhold' + 'Emne' as label + name (no word boundary, \s crosses lines), and the admin_date hits are government-document dates kept on purpose ('fastsatt av Kunnskapsdepartementet 7. juni 2016'). Outside the sample, at least 79 offerings lose the revision date of the national guidelines ('av 1. september 2016, revidert 17. oktober 2018' becomes 'revidert ,') because .not_gov is checked at the end of the date, which shrinks the 80-character window; about 45 plans from 2018 lose the year from fagplan URLs ('…/m5glu-fagplan-norsk-2018-2019').

findings.evidence: Redaksjonell endring foretatt , 29. januar;2020 og 23. november 2020
findings.description: The rubric says approval and editorial-change dates must go. Here only the first date of the stamp is removed. The raw line is 'Redaksjonell endring foretatt 17. desember 2019, 29. januar;2020 og 23. november 2020'. This is 1 of the 28 packet courses. A scan of all 1684 oslomet plans with the current code finds 48 offerings that keep an approval date on a stamp line. 6 have the same ';'-glued lists: M5GNA2100, M1GMT1100 and M1GNO1100 in 2022 ('lagt inn ,;25. november 2019, 23. november 2020 og 29. januar 2021', 'lagt inn , 19. april og;7. juni 2018;'). The other 42 are RLE fagplan offerings, for example oslomet_M5GRL2100-1_2019_spring_2 and oslomet_M1GRL2100-1_2023_autumn_1. In those, 'Revisjon godkjent av utdanningsutvalget 14. februar 2019 og på fullmakt av leder i utdanningsutvalget 4. mars 2019' keeps '4. mars 2019'. These dates are not personal data, but they date the plan version.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: There are two mechanisms in R/anonymize.R. (1) The 2022 site's ';' rendering artifact is glued into the date list ('januar;2020', 'og;7. juni'). .anon_oslomet() strips only ';' with whitespace on both sides. .long_dates_regex joins list items only with [ \t]*(,|og|and)[ \t]* and needs [ \t]+ before the year, so the list match stops after the first date. (2) The approval-date rule in .anon_generic() needs a keyword (godkjent|revisjon|foretatt|lagt inn|...) at the start of every match, and its prefix [^\n.]{0,100}? cannot pass a '.'. str_replace_all matches do not overlap, so once the first date run has used up the keyword, a later date on the same line has no keyword left. That is why '4. mars 2019' stays after '… og på fullmakt av leder i utdanningsutvalget', and why '23. november 2020' stays after the broken list.
findings.suggested_fix: (1) In .anon_oslomet(), before the generic rules run, turn glued semicolons into spaces: str_replace_all with regex (?<=[\p{L}\d.,:)]);+(?=[\p{L}\d]) -> ' '. Tested: 'Redaksjonell endring foretatt 17. desember 2019, 29. januar;2020 og 23. november 2020' becomes 'Redaksjonell endring foretatt'. (2) In .anon_generic(), repeat the approval-date str_replace_all until the text stops changing; the keyword is kept, so the next date matches on the next pass. Tested: a second pass removes '4. mars 2019' from the RLE line. Add both lines to tests/testthat/test-anonymize.R, run tar_make() and read metrics_check.

findings.description: This is a rendering artifact that the oslomet handler is meant to strip but removes only in part. The 2022 OsloMet site printed ';' in place of spaces. .anon_oslomet() drops ';' lines and ';' between spaces, so words stay glued: 'grunnlag;for', 'samt;vurdere nødvendige sikkerhetstiltak;', 'egnet;utstyr', 'fellesskap.;'. It shows in 5 of the 28 packet courses, all 2022 offerings (courses 7, 12, 18, 25 and 28). Across the institution, 124 of 1675 non-empty plans have a ';' between two letters: 120 of the 250 offerings from 2022 and 4 from 2021. This is not personal data, and most tokenizers split on ';'. But regex rules that need a space between words do not match across the glue, and that is what leaves the dates in the admin_date finding.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: .anon_oslomet() in R/anonymize.R has only str_remove_all('(?m)^\s*;\s*$') and str_remove_all('(?<=\s);(?=\s)'). No rule handles a ';' with a letter or digit on either side. The artifact is in the raw page text, so fulltext extraction passes it through.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the same rule as in the admin_date finding: in .anon_oslomet(), str_replace_all with regex (?<=[\p{L}\d.,:)]);+(?=[\p{L}\d]) -> ' ', then remove line-final runs after a full stop with (?m)(?<=\.);+[ \t]*$. Real semicolons are followed by a space ('fagstoffet; både') and are not touched. On the current data the letter;letter pattern occurs only in 2021-2022 plans. institution_sections() also calls anonymize_text(), so the sections get the fix too. Add a test case to tests/testthat/test-anonymize.R.
